To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the antinocicep-tive and cardiovascular effects of PAG activation are not mediated by activation of serotonergic neurons.

1) PAG stimulation activates nonserotonergic neurons in RM/NRCM but not serotonergic neurons, and 2) PAG stimulation does not excite serotonergic neurons in the ventral medulla, which are activated by stimulation of the rostral ventrolateral medulla (RVLM) or by stimulation in the caudal ventrolateral medullary region (CVLM).
serotonergic-like pontomedullary neurons are not activated by antinociceptivestimulation in the periaqueductalgrey.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neuroanatomical and neurochemical basis of pain modulation.
the neuroanatomical and neurochemical organization of the brainstem raphe nuclei and their role in pain processing and modulation.
the neuroanatomical and functional properties of the midbrain periaquetuctal gray matter (PAG) and its descending pathways, with particular reference to its role in pain and autonomic regulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pontomedullar raphe magnus and adjacent nucleus retcularis magnocellularis are not the site of the serotonergic neurons that mediate the effects of midbrain stimulation.
serotonergic neurons are not activated by antinociceptivestimulation in the PAG, and therefore are not necessary for antinocicepive effects of PAG activation.
serotonergic cells in the RM/NRMC are not activated by PAG stimulation, but this is not to say that the serotonergic cells do not participate in the antinociceptivenor cardiovascular effects of PAG.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PAG does not activate serotonergic cells at the level of the RM or NRMC, but does activate other cells in this region.
PAG stimulation does not excite serotonergic cells in the pontomedulla.
the PAG is a critical structure in the modulation of pain, and the PAG is also a critical structure in cardiovascular modulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neurons important in transmitting antinociceptivestimulation from the PAG to the rostral medulla are not serotonergic.
serotonergic cells in the pontine and medullary raphe nuclei are not involved in the transmission of antinociceptivetop-down signals from the periaqueductalgrey to the spinal cord.
serotonergic-like pontomedullary neurons are not activated by antinociceptic stimulation of the midbrain periaqductal gray.
